newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel mutual funds post biggest rise since 1994.
newsitem.headline: Israel mutual funds post biggest rise since 1994.

text.p: Israeli mutual fund assets posted their biggest monthly rise in three and a half years, rising 10.1 percent to 18.4 billion shekels ($5.2 billion) in June, Meitav Investments and Securities said in a report on Monday.
Meitav attributed the rise both to a large net inflow of capital in the month -- approximately 1.2 billion shekels -- and to high returns of 2.8 percent.

Most of the inflow was into unlinked bond funds, which raised a net 809 million shekels, due to the launching of three new funds in the category, Meitav said. It noted that unlinked bond funds had the lowest returns this year and were hit by the sharp depreciation of the shekel at the end of June.

Share funds raised a net 326 million shekels, compared with May's 85 million shekels and virtually nil in April. "This was the biggest (monthly) sum to be raised by share funds since the start of the stock market crisis at the beginning of 1994," Meitav noted.
It added that most of the money going into stock funds went into small capitalisation Karam funds and those specialising in finance and banking stocks.
Gidi Halpern, investment manager at Meitav, said the June figures do not yet point to a resurgence of broad public interest in the Israeli market.
"The public still has not come in," he said. "I suspect most of the money that went into the stock funds came from institutions, like provident funds."

Although the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange's Mishtanim index has risen in excess of 40 percent this year, Halpern said he did not expect small investors to enter the market until prices had risen considerably more.
